judgment.rationale: The report supplies a useful elevation-boundary reproduction. Reproduce cursor restoration versus immediate per-window repaint separately; ordinary elevated windows and the UAC secure desktop must not be conflated.
evidence: PowerToys0.102.3001; activate CursorHide, open Task Manager elevated, then move the pointer over it: the pointer reportedly stays invisible.
The supplied archive contains AutoHideCursor settings with hide_on_typing=true and hide_on_idle=false; the module-specific log entries do not identify a restore error.
The inspected implementation replaces system cursors and reloads them via SPI_SETCURSORS; RefreshCurrentCursor sends WM_NCHITTEST/WM_SETCURSOR to the window under the pointer.
The worker also polls cursor position on its timer, so a missing elevated hook callback alone is not a proven explanation.

title: CursorHide: no mouse cursor with elevated apps

setup: Use hide-on-typing enabled and hide-on-idle disabled, as supplied.
prerequisites: Controlled Windows test machine; preserve cursor scheme and module settings.
reproduce.title: Separate system-cursor restore from elevated-window repaint
steps: 1. Type to hide the pointer, move over an ordinary window and record recovery.
2. Repeat over elevated Task Manager, with PowerToys non-elevated and then elevated; record which boundary fails.
3. Capture SPI_SETCURSORS result/error and refresh-message outcomes; disable CursorHide and confirm the configured cursor returns.
4. Exercise UAC secure-desktop entry/exit separately, without treating it as an ordinary elevated window.
reproduce.expected_result: Pointer visibility recovers on movement and module disable without requiring privileged input or replacing the user cursor scheme permanently.
